steps_done: 1. Opened /d/dss-sf-2026/ at 1440x900 in an isolated agent-browser session (qa5main). The default session is shared with other QA agents and its snapshot showed another agent's focus page. main-01 was taken before the thumbnails finished loading, so main-01b was taken after they loaded.

2. Clicked slide 4, then shift-clicked slide 6. agent-browser keydown Shift + click selected only slide 6. A synthetic click event with shiftKey set gave the range 4-6: the context chip reads 'slides 4–6', the caption under the filmstrip reads 'slides 4–6', and three previews show (main-02).

3. Pressed End on the canvas: scrollLeft went to 2000 (the max). The filmstrip shows slides 22-30, and '+21' moved to the left side, which is the correct count. Home brings it back to 0 (main-03, main-03b).

4. Remark cards have no 'info' control. Clicking the remark text expands it (aria-expanded=true) (main-04-info). Resolved the slide 3/4 remark: the header went from 67 to 66 and the badges on slides 4, 5 and 6 each dropped by 1 (main-04).

5. Clicked 'open lane' on the slide 6 JSON remark. The lane 'Split request and response onto two slides' was created as the first lane row, below the 4-6 previews and off-screen. It only became visible after I scrolled it into view (main-05).

6. Refused 'modify slide 6': the card greys out with 'refused' and there is no new version (main-06a-refuse). Accepted 'insert slide 7': the rail shows v20 'added "The response answers in the same shape"' and the header shows v20 / 31 slides (main-06b-accept). A few seconds later the lane row closed (main-06b-accept-later).

7. Selected slide 2 and sent 'Make the title of this slide shorter, five words max.' The co-author answered in about 24 s: the title is already 4 words, so it opened no lane, and the thread says so. No lane appeared, which is correct (main-07-before, main-07).
8. Escape cleared the selection to 'whole deck' (main-08-esc). After reselecting slide 2, a click on empty canvas also cleared it (main-08).

Caveat: other agents were changing the same deck during this run (v17 to v20, new lanes 'back to v17' and 'Shorter labels on the four layers', remark count 67 to 66 to 67 to 69). Some count changes may come from them.

bugs.where: MAIN canvas, range-selection previews while the canvas is scrolled horizontally
bugs.what: The selected-slide previews scroll horizontally with the filmstrip instead of staying in place. At the right end, the slide 4 and slide 6 previews are cut off at the left edge ('4: A loop with one slow step', '6: Typed in, typed out' with the left part missing) and now sit under the columns for slides 22-27, which suggests the wrong slides.
bugs.repro: Open /d/dss-sf-2026/, click slide 4, shift-click slide 6, focus the canvas and press End.
bugs.expected: Previews stay pinned (or move as one block) and are never cut off. Only the filmstrip and lane columns scroll.

bugs.where: MAIN lane row after accepting a change
bugs.what: Right after a click on accept, the lane row still shows the accepted card with live ✓/✗ buttons and the leftover 'refused' label, for about 3-7 s, until the lane closes. Clicking a second time in that window could accept or refuse something already settled. A red move-connector line is also drawn vertically across the whole canvas (x≈838, y 175 to 760), through unrelated lane rows.
bugs.repro: Open a lane with two changes from a remark ('open lane' on the slide 6 JSON remark). Refuse 'modify slide 6', then accept 'insert slide 7', and take a screenshot within 3 s.
bugs.expected: The accepted card switches to 'accepted' (or the lane closes) at once, with no active buttons. Connectors stay inside their own lane row.

bugs.where: MAIN lane 'Open the memory answer before the coordination block'
bugs.what: The lane shows a settled 'accepted' tag for a no-op change. Its title attribute is 'move slide 8, Three read patterns, one log, to 8'. The tag hangs under a context thumbnail, and the lane's change list does not mention it.
bugs.repro: Open /, look at the 'Open the memory answer…' lane row: the text 'accepted' sits under the slide-8 thumbnail column. Inspect [data-testid=settled-tag]: its title is 'move slide 8 … to 8'.
bugs.expected: No move change is created when the target position equals the source. Any accepted change shown in the row should also be listed in the row's text.

bugs.where: MAIN, 'open lane' from a remark while a slide is selected
bugs.what: After 'open lane', the new lane is placed as the first lane row, but that row is below the 550px selection previews, under the fold. The canvas does not scroll to it. The only feedback is the remark card switching to 'lane opened: …'; nothing changes on the visible canvas.
bugs.repro: Select slides 4-6 and click 'open lane' on the slide 6 JSON remark in the thread. The visible canvas still shows only the previews (same view as main-04). Scroll down to find the lane (main-05).
bugs.expected: The canvas scrolls to the new lane row and briefly highlights it, or the remark's 'lane opened' link jumps there.

bugs.where: Thread history on slide 2
bugs.what: Earlier co-author replies in this thread (08:07 PM and 08:56 PM) are in French although the user wrote in English. One of them shows a raw internal lane id: 'Lane l__w9KF0bWiS : le titre passe à « One answer already exists »…'. These messages come from an earlier round, but they are stored and shown to every reader.
bugs.repro: Select slide 2 and scroll the thread up to the 08:07 PM co-author message.
bugs.expected: Replies come in the user's language and refer to lanes by name, never by internal id.

bugs.where: MAIN remark counts (header vs filmstrip badges vs thread)
bugs.what: The counts do not reconcile. The header says 67 open remarks, but the per-slide badges in main-01 add up to 97. With slides 4-6 selected, the badges total 11 while the thread lists 3 + '4 more remarks' = 7. Resolving one remark that names slides 3 and 4 decremented the badges on 4, 5 and 6 but not on 3. About a minute later the header went back to 67 and a reworded slide 3 remark had appeared; other agents running checks may explain part of this.
bugs.repro: Open / and add up the filmstrip badges, then compare with the header. Select slides 4-6 and compare the badge total with the thread count. Click 'resolve' on 'slide 3 (One log…) states the whole answer…, then slide 4…' and watch the badges on slides 3-6.
bugs.expected: Each badge counts the remarks that the thread lists for that slide. The header total equals the number of distinct remarks and is labelled as such. Resolving a remark updates exactly the slides it names.

bugs.where: MAIN filmstrip left overflow marker
bugs.what: When the canvas is scrolled, the '+2' marker on the left overlaps a partly hidden red badge from slide 2 (a half circle with '6' cut at x≈148).
bugs.repro: Select slides 4-6 and scroll the lane 'Split request…' into view: the canvas scrolls left by two columns.
bugs.expected: The overflow marker hides or masks thumbnails and badges that are partly off-screen.

frictions.what: There is no 'info' affordance. Details open by clicking the truncated remark text, and nothing tells you that text is clickable: no chevron, no hover state. I found it through aria-expanded.
frictions.expected: A visible 'more' or chevron control on truncated remarks.

frictions.what: 'resolve' takes effect at once, with no undo, toast or confirmation. The card just disappears and the count drops.
frictions.expected: A short undo toast ('Remark resolved · undo').

frictions.what: In the 'Split request and response' lane, refusing 'modify slide 6' and accepting 'insert slide 7' is allowed without any warning. The result is a duplicate: slide 6 keeps both JSON cards and the new slide 7 repeats the response. Another open lane ('Drop the classifier wire-format slide') still proposes removing slide 6, and nothing flags the conflict.
frictions.expected: Warn when the changes in a lane depend on each other, and flag lanes that touch the same slides.

frictions.what: Selecting a single slide shows a preview about 550px tall that pushes every lane row below the versions rail. The next lane name ('back to v17') peeks out at y≈777, cut off by the rail. With a selection, you cannot see the lanes and the slide at the same time.
frictions.expected: A smaller preview, or lanes for the selected slide visible next to it.

frictions.what: The 'all slides' grid under the lanes repeats the filmstrip with truncated titles ('2 One home alr…'), and its last row is cut off by the versions rail.
frictions.expected: One slide index, not two.

frictions.what: The width of the lane name column depends on where the lane's first card is. 'Shorter labels on the four layers' wraps onto 3 lines next to a card at column 5, while other lanes use one line.
frictions.expected: A fixed-width lane header column.

frictions.what: Shift-click sent through agent-browser (keydown Shift + click) selected only slide 6. A range only worked with a synthetic click event that had shiftKey set. This may be a limit of the tool and not of the app, so it is unconfirmed. There is no other visible way to select a range.
frictions.expected: Shift-click or a drag across the filmstrip reliably selects a range.

frictions.what: Messages from different sessions show only times (08:07 PM, 10:29 PM, 12:33 AM) with no date or day separator, so the order across days is unclear.
frictions.expected: Day separators or dates on older messages.

steps_done: 1. Opened /, clicked slide 5, pressed Enter: /slide/s_LNLSV_dFNk, header 'slide 5 of 30, Few decisions need an LLM', render, story, notes, empty lanes, remarks, empty thread (slide-01)
2. ArrowRight x2 then ArrowLeft x1: URL went s_DV8xMaExQd → s_WJND20RDFq → s_DV8xMaExQd and header followed to 'slide 6 of 30, Typed in, typed out' (slide-02)

3a. Sent 'Replace the diagram labels with shorter ones, keep the meaning.' on slide 6, where step 2 left off. Answer took about 20 s and opened no lane: slide 6 has no diagram, only JSON. Nothing new under 'lanes on this slide' and the render is unchanged (slide-03-pending, slide-03)

3b. Sent the same message on slide 5, which has a diagram. Answer took about 80 s and opened lane 'Shorter labels on the four layers'. The lane appeared under 'lanes on this slide', the thread names it and shows a main/proposed render pair with accept/refuse, the big render switched to 'proposed in ...', and story/notes are marked 'in <lane>, unchanged' (slide-03b, slide-03c)

4. Clicked 'open in focus' on the lane row in the right column: went to /lane/l_Z5Xtq2OzCX/change/c_VUD7mw2xS5 with main and lane side by side, the lane thread carried over, slide 5 highlighted in the strip (slide-04). Browser back returned to /slide/s_LNLSV_dFNk (slide-05)
5. Escape from the slide page: went to /d/dss-sf-2026/ with slide 5 still selected in the strip, big render and right panel 'slide 5' (slide-06). Scrolled to the lane rows on main (slide-06b)
6. Opened /slide/s_doesNotExist123: bare page with one sentence and a 'back to main' link (slide-07)

bugs.where: /slide/<missing id> (slide-07)
bugs.what: A slide id that never existed gets the message 'This slide is no longer on main: a change removed it, or the link is out of date.' That claims the slide used to exist. The page also has no deck title, no header and no slide count. It is a blank page with one line of text.
bugs.repro: Open http://127.0.0.1:4177/d/dss-sf-2026/slide/s_doesNotExist123
bugs.expected: Separate 'no slide with this id in this deck' from 'removed by version vN'. Keep the normal deck header and offer the nearest slide or the strip.

bugs.where: Lane change text on main, and remarks/lane rows that cite slides
bugs.what: User-facing change rationales show raw internal slide ids instead of slide numbers and titles. Examples: 'the response JSON cut from s_DV8xMaExQd gets its own stage', 'keeps s_1bPtQ4g3u6 attached to the read-pattern it details', 's_sdB7-sjwth is the code for the private tier of s_1bPtQ4g3u6', 's_q3tV81Agum continues the tiers'. Other rationales on the same screen do resolve ids to 'slide 5, Few decisions need an LLM', so this is inconsistent.
bugs.repro: Open /, press Escape so nothing is selected, and scroll to the lane rows under the big render. Read the 'Split request and response onto two slides' and 'Open the memory answer before the coordination block' rows.
bugs.expected: Every s_xxx reference is rendered as 'slide N (Title)'.

bugs.where: Slide 6 render while a 'remove' lane is pending (slide-02, slide-03-pending)
bugs.what: The 'removed in lane Drop the classifier wire-format slide' badge sits in the middle of the render and covers the JSON. It hides part of the '"probabilities"' key and the '"choice"' line. When the page is scrolled the badge sticks to the top of the viewport and keeps covering content.
bugs.repro: Go to /slide/s_DV8xMaExQd (slide 6) and look at the main render. Then scroll the conversation.
bugs.expected: Show the removal as a corner tag or in the frame header, not over the slide content.

bugs.where: Slide-page thread, lane card in the reply (slide-03c)
bugs.what: The lane card in the co-author reply has an empty 'body:' label with nothing after it. The next line is a raw asset path, 'assets: assets/s04.png → assets/gen-mup1dlwr-m8p1s0.png', which is internal filesystem noise. The focus view shows the same change as '[image: s04.png] → [image: gen-...png]'.
bugs.repro: On /slide/s_LNLSV_dFNk send 'Replace the diagram labels with shorter ones, keep the meaning.', wait for the reply and scroll to its lane card.
bugs.expected: Hide empty fields. Show 'image regenerated' instead of file paths.

bugs.where: Slide 6 thread history (slide-02 snapshot)
bugs.what: Two older co-author replies to an English message are in French ('Cette slide n'a pas de diagramme…', 'Tu me le redemandes…'). The later replies are in English. The reply language does not follow the user's language.
bugs.repro: Open /slide/s_DV8xMaExQd and scroll the conversation to the top. The 08:54 PM and 08:56 PM co-author replies are French; the user messages are English.
bugs.expected: The co-author always answers in the user's language.

bugs.where: Slide 6 co-author reply at 12:30 AM (slide-03)
bugs.what: The co-author says 'this is the third time round on the same slide'. The thread shows the identical request 5 times (08:53, 08:54, 09:41, 10:26, 12:29). The reply also never mentions the open lane 'Drop the classifier wire-format slide', which would remove this slide entirely, so it is the most relevant fact.
bugs.repro: On /slide/s_DV8xMaExQd send 'Replace the diagram labels with shorter ones, keep the meaning.' and read the reply.
bugs.expected: Count the earlier requests correctly and mention open lanes that touch the slide.

bugs.where: Slide 5 notes after the label lane (slide-03b)
bugs.what: Story and notes are marked 'in Shorter labels on the four layers, unchanged'. The lane renames 'generative agent' to 'LLM' and 'learned model' to 'learned', but the notes still describe 'a generative agent' and 'a learned decision model' card by card. The co-author also says the generated image dropped the card panels on 3 of 4 columns and asks the user to re-request. That is a known visual regression shipped inside the proposal.
bugs.repro: On slide 5 send the label request, then compare the proposed render with main and read the notes.
bugs.expected: The lane updates the notes wording to match the new labels and does not propose a render with a regression it already detected.

frictions.what: Arrow navigation in step 2 lands on slide 6, a JSON slide with no diagram, so 'replace the diagram labels' never produces a lane there. The user has to know which slides have diagrams. The thread also shows 5 identical requests with near-identical refusals, and nothing de-duplicates them or collapses old exchanges.
frictions.expected: Collapse older exchanges. When the co-author refuses, offer one-click alternatives (e.g. 'propose: drop probabilities block').

frictions.where: Slide page after browser back from focus (slide-05)
frictions.what: Before opening focus, the render toggle showed 'proposed in Shorter labels…'. After browser back it reset to 'main', so the user's place is lost.
frictions.expected: Keep the render toggle state across back navigation.

frictions.what: 'remarks on this slide' lists deck-level remarks about slides 2/3 ordering, with 'lane opened: Open the memory answer before the coordination block'. That lane does not touch slide 5, and 'lanes on this slide' says no lane changes it. The remarks list also changed between visits (2 → 3 items, different texts) because background checks were running, with no indication that it refreshed.
frictions.expected: Show only remarks that concern this slide, or group cross-slide remarks separately. Signal when remarks get regenerated.

frictions.what: The thread and its lane card are capped at about 600 px while the column is about 1030 px wide, so the main/proposed thumbnails in the reply are tiny and the text wraps early. Once the conversation grows, the big render scrolls out of view and the 'main / proposed in …' toggle disappears with it.
frictions.expected: Use the available width for render comparisons, or keep the toggle sticky.

frictions.where: Slide page lane row accessible names (slide-02)
frictions.what: On slide 6 the remove-lane buttons are labelled 'accept: remove slide 6, a slide' / 'refuse: remove slide 6, a slide'. The title is replaced by the placeholder 'a slide'. The main page labels the same lane 'remove slide 6, Typed in, typed out'.
frictions.expected: Use the slide title consistently.

frictions.what: The deck version moved v17 → v18 → v19 under me ('reverted body, assets of slide 9', 'moved Private state, compacted'), with slide numbers in lane rows shifting (slide 9 → slide 10), and nothing told me. A lane header 'back to v17' with a lone '+1' sits half-hidden behind the fixed versions band.
frictions.expected: A visible 'deck changed (v19), N slides renumbered' notice. Lanes are not occluded by the versions band.

steps_done: Opened / at 1440x900 in an isolated agent-browser session (the default session was shared: its URL jumped to /slide/s_LNLSV_dFNk while I was working, so another agent was driving it). Lanes were open: 'Open the memory answer before the coordination block' (moves) and 'Drop the classifier wire-format slide'.

Tried to click a lane cell for the move lane. Its 4 pending cells are drawn at x=1675-2048 px, off-screen behind the sidebar, so they cannot be clicked. Clicked the change line 'move slide 17 ... to 9' instead and landed on /lane/l_xkkuRHenRf/change/c_UGyg5caeTI (focus-01).

Read the focus view: a 'main, was 17' row and a 'this lane, now 9' row with neighbours, the diff line 'move keeps slide 17 ... details', the actions (previous change / accept / refuse / next change), the bottom slide strip and the 'changes in this lane' list.
Clicked next change: now on change 2 of 4, URL c_eiTR9-R0_h (focus-02). Clicked previous change: back to change 1, where 'previous change' is disabled at opacity 0.4 (focus-03).

Sent 'Also change the story line to mention Kafka Streams.' in the lane thread. A 'co-author is working on slide 17' status with a timer showed while it worked; the reply took about 70 s. The co-author added a 7th change ('modify slide 17') to the same lane and the header count went from 'of 4' to 'of 5' (focus-04).

Accepted the current change (move 17 to 9). The screen stayed on the same change and showed 'accepted (v19)', before/after cards and a 'next change' button (focus-05; settled state in focus-05b-settled).

Clicked next change (focus-05c-next) and refused it (move Latest value per key). The screen stayed on the change and showed 'refused' and 'next change' (focus-06). After the refuse, changes 4 and 5 showed 'accepted' even though I never accepted them. Checked them in a second session (focus-06b-change4-false-accepted) and against main's history.
Set the viewport to 1200x800 and reloaded (focus-07). Scrolled to the lane thread (focus-07b-thread-scrolled). Went back to 1440 and reloaded to compare (focus-07c-1440-reload).

bugs.where: focus: refuse action / 'changes in this lane' list
bugs.what: Refusing change 3 (move 'Latest value per key') silently closed changes 4 and 5 (move 'Streams builds, agents read', move 'One KTable, one query') as 'accepted'. Nothing was applied to main: main history has no version for them (v19 is my accept, v20 is an unrelated slide add), and the slides stay at positions 20 and 21. The focus page for change 4 says 'This change is accepted.' and 'main, slide 20, accepted'. The strip still paints 20 and 21 as changed (red). The only explanation is a co-author message at the bottom of the thread: 'Moving slide 20 ...: already on main, nothing to decide.' The user's choice was refuse; the lane's intended order (the Streams tier right after the private tier) was dropped and the change was relabelled as an acceptance.
bugs.repro: 1. Open lane l_xkkuRHenRf ('Open the memory answer before the coordination block') with pending moves 17→9, 18→10, 19→11, 20→12. 2. In focus, accept 'move slide 17'. 3. Click next change, then refuse 'move slide 18 (Latest value per key)'. 4. Look at the right list: items 4 and 5 now say 'accepted'. 5. Open /d/dss-sf-2026/lane/l_xkkuRHenRf/change/c_GMhtAwdNKC: header says 'accepted'. 6. Open / and check the versions: no version for these moves; slides 20 and 21 are not moved.
bugs.expected: Changes made obsolete by a refuse should be marked as such (eg 'dropped: no longer applies after refusing #3') or stay pending for a decision. Never 'accepted' when nothing was written to main. The screen should also say right away which other changes the refuse affected.

bugs.where: focus at 1200x800: lane thread
bugs.what: At 1200x800 the 'changes in this lane' list is gone entirely, with no toggle to bring it back. The conversation drops below the canvas and you only reach it by scrolling the main pane. At 1440 after the same reload, the list is there.
bugs.repro: 1. Open /d/dss-sf-2026/lane/l_xkkuRHenRf/change/c_eiTR9-R0_h. 2. agent-browser set viewport 1200 800, then reload. 3. The snapshot's 'lane thread' region has only 'conversation about this lane'; there is no 'changes in this lane' region. 4. Set the viewport to 1440 900 and reload: the 'changes in this lane' region is back.
bugs.expected: The list of changes stays available at laptop width (stacked, collapsible, or in a drawer). It is the only way to jump to a specific change or see the accepted/refused state.

bugs.where: main view: move-lane row (entry point to focus)
bugs.what: The move lane's 4 pending change cells are rendered at x=1675-2048 px with a 1440 viewport, off-canvas and under the sidebar. The visible row shows only the slide-8 thumbnail, a '+4' that is a plain span (not clickable), and an 'accepted' label floating about 70 px below the thumbnail. You cannot click a pending cell to reach focus.
bugs.repro: 1. At 1440x900 open /d/dss-sf-2026/. 2. Find the lane 'Open the memory answer before the coordination block'. 3. Try to click one of its change cells: only the slide-8 thumbnail and '+4' are visible, and '+4' does nothing. 4. Eval the bounding rects of the a[href*='/lane/'] links: x is at least 1675.
bugs.expected: Pending change cells are visible or reachable (scroll, or '+4' expands or links to the first pending change).
bugs.screenshot: focus-01.png (initial main capture, overwritten by the focus screen; the geometry comes from the DOM eval)

bugs.where: focus header vs 'changes in this lane' list numbering
bugs.what: The header counts only pending changes ('change 1 of 4') while the list numbers every change (the same change is item '2'), so the two numbers never match. On change 2 the header says 'change 2 of 4' and the list highlights '3'.
bugs.repro: 1. Open /d/dss-sf-2026/lane/l_xkkuRHenRf/change/c_UGyg5caeTI before any decision. 2. The header says 'change 1 of 4' and the highlighted list item is numbered 2.
bugs.expected: One numbering scheme, or a header that says '1 of 4 pending'.

bugs.where: focus right list after accept
bugs.what: Right after clicking accept, the list item for the accepted change still has no 'accepted' badge and the strip still shows the old positions (17 current). Both update a few seconds later, after the deck renumbers.
bugs.repro: 1. On change 'move slide 17', click accept. 2. Screenshot within about 2 s: the header says 'accepted (v19)' but list item 2 has no badge and the strip marks 17. 3. Snapshot again a few seconds later: item 2 says 'accepted' and the strip shows 9/10.
bugs.expected: The list, header and strip update together when the accept call returns.

bugs.where: lane thread: co-author reply rendering
bugs.what: Markdown is only partly rendered: the blockquote shows as a literal '> Private task state ...' line while the bold inside it renders. Separately, the change cards attached to the reply (main/proposed thumbnails, 'move: keeps s_1bPtQ4g3u6 attached...') are shown live but disappear after a reload. The live card also leaks a raw slide id (s_1bPtQ4g3u6), and the main view's change lines leak ids too (s_sdB7-sjwth, s_q3tV81Agum, s_6q7kZ4ZqHG).
bugs.repro: 1. In the lane thread, send 'Also change the story line to mention Kafka Streams.' 2. Wait for the reply: a literal '>' appears and the cards show a raw id in 'move: keeps s_1bPtQ4g3u6 ...'. 3. Reload: the cards are gone and only text remains.
bugs.expected: Full markdown rendering, the same message content before and after reload, and slide titles/positions instead of internal ids.

bugs.where: focus canvas neighbour rows
bugs.what: Neighbour thumbnails in the 'this lane' row (and in the 'main' row on the accepted/refused screens) are cut off at the left and right edges ('e log has three jobs', 'ree read patterns, one log', 'Streams builds, agents re', 'vate state, compacted'). The neighbour grid is also ordered column-first (13,15 / 14,16), which is hard to read.
bugs.repro: Open any change in focus at 1440x900 and look at the left and right neighbour columns of the 'this lane, now N' row.
bugs.expected: Neighbours fully visible (smaller) and in reading order.

frictions.what: The revision happened in place (same lane, new change #7 'modify slide 17'), but the only signals were the chat text and the header count changing from 'of 4' to 'of 5'. The list did not scroll to or highlight #7, the canvas stayed on the move change, and nothing on the slide-17 card says it now has a second pending change. The thread had auto-scrolled to the middle of the reply, so the 'Added to ... as a seventh change' sentence was off-screen.
frictions.expected: A visible 'new change #7 added to this lane' toast or highlight with a jump link, and the thread scrolled to the start of the reply.

frictions.what: For a move, the before/after cards show the same slide twice. After accepting, 'before, slide 17' and 'now in main as v19' are identical images and neither gives the new position. The change labels also renumber as main changes ('move slide 17' became 'move slide 10', 'move slide 18' became 'move slide 19'), and the 'to N' target is lost from the list.
frictions.expected: Moves show 'from 17 to 9' explicitly and keep stable labels (title plus from→to).

frictions.what: Enabled 'next change' and 'previous change' are grey text links in the same colour as their disabled state; disabled differs only by opacity 0.4. That is distinguishable but weak, and the enabled ones read as captions rather than buttons.
frictions.expected: Button styling for the enabled nav and a clearly different disabled state.

frictions.what: The list scrolls inside a fixed 404 px box (scrollHeight 610) with no scroll cue. Changes #5 to #7, including the refused one and the newly added one, are hidden below the fold.
frictions.expected: A visible scroll affordance or a count of the hidden items, or auto-scroll to the active and newest items.

frictions.what: A struck-through number (21, later 22) marks a refused change, with no legend or tooltip. Accepted and pending changes are painted the same red.
frictions.expected: A legend or tooltip, and distinct colours for accepted, pending and refused.

frictions.what: After a refuse the screen shows side-by-side 'main, kept' / 'refused proposal' cards. After a reload, the same URL shows a different layout (strips plus 'This change is refused. Review the first pending change').
frictions.expected: The same view for the same state with or without a reload.

frictions.what: A one-line story edit took about 70 s to come back.
frictions.expected: Faster turnaround, or a progress hint with more than a timer.

critique.verdict: Two screens follow the principle and two break it. Focus and the slide page do it right: the slide sits in the middle, the proposal renders on it, and accept/refuse sits under it. The main screen, where the creator spends most of his time, still has the mockup-era right bar, and that bar is now mostly a feed of 67 machine remarks rather than a conversation. A single proposed change shows up in three or four places: a lane row on main, a lane card on the slide page, a mini compare inside the reply, and the focus view. Each place has its own accept button, so his attention scatters instead of staying on the slide. Lane rows on main are blocks of text with internal IDs (s_1bPtQ4g3u6) and one stray thumbnail. They are not the card-per-change strip from the mockup, so he reads prose to understand a move he should see. The deck also changes under him (v17 → v20, slides renumbered) without telling him, and the fixed versions band covers the lanes. The co-author's thinking is the strongest part: it pushes back, names tradeoffs and refuses no-op requests. The workbench around it still makes him hunt for where his answer landed.

principle_violations.what: The conversation lives in a 360px right bar, and with no selection it opens on a remark feed ('67 open remarks on the deck', each with propose/resolve/warn), not on the conversation. When he selects slide 2, the big render sits in the middle but the co-author's answer appears in the right bar (main-07), away from the slide.
principle_violations.why_it_hurts: This is the exact layout the creator rejected. He reads the slide in the centre and the answer at the far right, and remarks push his own messages below the fold (main-07-before shows remarks plus story plus notes before any message).

principle_violations.what: Lane rows are text lists ('move slide 17, Private state, compacted, to 9: keeps s_1bPtQ4g3u6 attached to the read-pattern it details'). They show one thumbnail at the column of the first card plus '+4', and internal slide IDs leak into the rationale. The mockup's arc for a move and its row of cards with ✓/✗ under each are gone.
principle_violations.why_it_hurts: He cannot see a change, only read about it, and the IDs are noise that belongs to the model. Four moves read as four lines of jargon, not as one visual reorder.

principle_violations.what: With a slide selected, the 550px render plus the previous/next rail pushes every lane below the fixed versions band. 'back to v17' and 'Mentoring' peek out half-covered (main-07, home-07b, slide-06).
principle_violations.why_it_hurts: The pending proposals for the slide he is looking at are hidden right when he is deciding about it. The whole point of the canvas is to see slide and proposals together.

principle_violations.what: Main shows the same deck twice (filmstrip and the 'all slides' grid) plus red remark-count badges on every thumbnail (6, 5, 2, 7...). These counts use the same red as pending-change markers.
principle_violations.why_it_hurts: His attention goes to red counts of machine critiques rather than to his decisions. Remarks and proposals look alike, so he cannot tell what needs a decision from what is commentary.

principle_violations.what: Accepting in one lane changes the version (v18 → v20) and renumbers slides in every other lane ('slide 9' becomes 'slide 10' or 'slide 11') with no notice. The partial accept in 'Split request and response' gives a duplicated slide without any warning, and another lane still proposes removing that same slide.
principle_violations.why_it_hurts: The answer to his action lands somewhere he is not looking, and part of it lands nowhere at all. He finds out about collateral changes only by comparing numbers.

principle_violations.what: The conversation sits under the render, which is right, but in a ~600px column with its own nested scroll inside a scrolling page. When a lane comes back, the reply contains a second, thumbnail-sized main/proposed compare with its own accept/refuse, while the big render above has a toggle and the right column has a third lane card with ✓/✗.
principle_violations.why_it_hurts: There are three accept controls for one change. Once he scrolls to read the reply, the big render and its toggle scroll away, so he judges the change on 180px thumbnails.

principle_violations.what: 'remarks on this slide' lists deck-level remarks about slides 2/3 and 'lane opened: Open the memory answer…' on slide 5. Story and notes diffs strike out words one by one, leaving 'the', 'was' and 'free' as islands.
principle_violations.why_it_hurts: The right column is mostly unrelated commentary, and the before/after text cannot be read as sentences. The creator has to rebuild both versions in his head.

principle_violations.what: When he messages the lane, the reply appears in the right sidebar thread, and the revision (new change #7) lands in a list that does not scroll to it. The canvas stays on the move. After accept, the move diff shows two identical images ('before, slide 17' / 'now in main as v19').
principle_violations.why_it_hurts: The answer to his message is not shown where the change is. For a move, the after-accept view shows nothing about the move itself.

principle_violations.what: The same state has two different layouts: side-by-side 'main, kept / refused proposal' right after acting, and strips plus 'This change is refused. Review the first pending change' after a reload.
principle_violations.why_it_hurts: The screen looks different each time he lands on the same thing, which erodes trust in what he is seeing.

principle_violations.what: The outline answer repeats 10 inserts as large cards, each beside an empty dashed 'not in main' box, in the right bar. The same lane sits in the strip with its own ✓/✗. Present is the primary orange button on a 0-slide deck, and there is no 'draft outline from brief' starter.
principle_violations.why_it_hurts: His first experience is a long scroll of duplicated proposals in the side bar, with two places to act on the same slide.

principle_violations.what: Checks run one after another for ~5 min, re-run silently after any deck change ('running after a deck change'), and produce paragraph-long remarks. The status vocabulary varies: lane ready, open draft lane, draft ready, lane opened, propose, open lane.
principle_violations.why_it_hurts: The brief screen feeds the remark flood on main without saying what it is doing. Status words that read like buttons make him wonder whether something is waiting for him.

changes.change: Move the conversation into the canvas on main, as the slide page already does. When a slide or range is selected, the stack under the big render becomes: lane rows that touch this slide (inline), then the conversation for this context with full canvas width, then the input. Keep a whole-deck conversation under the filmstrip when nothing is selected. Remove the right bar. Remarks become a collapsed 'N remarks' chip on the selected slide's header, expanding inline, and the per-thumbnail remark badges go away (one grey dot at most). Shrink the selected-slide render to ~360px tall, put previous/next as small arrows, and make the versions band a single collapsible line that scrolls with the page, not a fixed footer.
changes.rationale: This is the creator's own principle, and main is where he spends his time. It removes the side-bar eye travel, puts proposals next to the slide they change, and stops 67 remarks from crowding out his messages.

changes.change: Render lane rows as in mockup 1. Use a fixed 220px header column (name, origin, discard). Next to it, one card per change aligned under its filmstrip column: proposed render, ✓/✗ under it, insert marked with +, removal as a dashed card, moves drawn as an arc from the old to the new column with a 'from 17 → 9' label. The rationale goes into a hover/expand line under the card, rewritten in slide titles. Strip every internal id (s_xxx) server-side before display. Delete the 'all slides' grid.
changes.rationale: He can see a change instead of reading it. Moves and reorders, which are most of the arc-check lanes, become visible at a glance, and the duplicate slide index disappears.

changes.change: Give each change exactly one place to act: the render it changes. Co-author replies that open or revise a lane show a one-line receipt in the thread ('Lane Shorter labels · 1 change · shown on the slide above ↑'). Clicking it scrolls to the render and flashes the proposed overlay. Remove the inline mini main/proposed compare and its accept/refuse from replies, and remove the empty 'not in main' boxes. Insert-only outlines become a compact title list in the reply that points to the strip. On the slide page, drop the right-column lane card's ✓/✗ and keep only the toggle plus accept/refuse under the render. Make the main/proposed toggle sticky at the top of the scroll area.
changes.rationale: Today one change has three or four accept buttons and two thumbnail sizes. One action surface on the big render means he judges at full size and always knows which control counts.

changes.change: Announce what moved, in place. After any accept, revise or background version bump, show a one-line notice at the top of the canvas: 'v19 → v20 · slide 17 moved to 9, slides 9–16 shifted by one · undo'. Flash the affected thumbnails for 2s. In focus, a lane revision scrolls the change list to the new item, selects it on the canvas, scrolls the thread to the start of the reply, and labels it 'new'. Moves keep stable labels (title + from→to) instead of renumbering. Before a partial accept, warn when changes in a lane depend on each other, and badge lanes that touch the same slide ('conflicts with Drop the classifier slide').
changes.rationale: Right now, the answer to his action often lands where he is not looking, or is not shown at all. Renumbering and conflicts silently produce wrong decks (duplicate slide 6/7).

changes.change: Cut remark noise to what concerns him. Run checks in parallel, with one overall progress line ('3 of 4 checks done'). Skip checks whose inputs have not changed. Show remarks only on the slides they cite, with cross-slide remarks grouped under the range header. Collapse 'info'-level remarks by default. Use one status vocabulary: 'lane open' for the status and a 'propose' button only. In story/notes diffs, show old and new as whole sentences when more than ~40% of the words change.
changes.rationale: Remarks are today's main source of misdirected attention: deck-level ones on unrelated slides, silent re-runs, and status labels that look like buttons. Fewer, better-placed remarks free the canvas for the conversation.

keep: Focus screen layout: big main-vs-lane render with neighbouring slides on both strips ('main, was 17' / 'this lane, now 9') is the best move visualisation in the tool, plus the numbered change list, the accept/refuse bar and the slide-number strip
Slide page puts the conversation under the render with a main/proposed toggle, the closest screen to the creator's principle
Dashed 'removed' overlay drawn directly on the slide render with 'removed in lane <name>' label
In-place working indicator 'co-author is working on slide 6 0:02' in the thread
Co-author's pushback quality: refuses no-op requests, names the cost of each alternative, flags arc conflicts before building ('Flagging one thing: this slide is the problem statement…')
Per-card accepted/refused states left visible in the lane row instead of the card disappearing
History compare: two version rows with connector lines, 'modified'/'moved from 15' labels, big side-by-side render, What changed list with per-row restore and inline confirm
'Open vN as a lane' as the way to restore, so a restore is reviewable like any proposal
Lane origin line ('from check: arc', 'from your request on slide 5', 'from history v17'), which tells him who proposed it
Restrained light theme with one accent colour reserved for proposals and actions
